cover.prose:
The source image — an isometric block city over a strategy-breeding harness — works because of three quiet decisions, and only one of them is the city: it maps roles in a mechanism rather than files; it spends its one visual scalar (height) on a true quantity; and it keeps a CONDITION field that says what is currently wrong. This set keeps those three decisions and lets everything else change with altitude.

The result is an argument about form: a loop where there is a genuine cycle (sheet 1), panels where packages are too small to be cities (sheet 2), the full city where the measurement thesis is actually true (sheet 3), a massed spine where the family shares one core but the limbs never touch (sheet 4), a chart where edges would be fiction (sheet 5), and mostly prose where only a definition survives (sheet 6). Fitness peaks in the middle altitudes and collapses at both ends.

Above the sixth altitude the set stops arguing about form and starts measuring. Sheets 7–10 are a survey quartet, each counting the same subject at a different boundary: what the repository holds (the monorepo by mass), what npm delivers (the sample app's node_modules, 297× the app it serves), what the browser downloads (the docs deploy on the wire, where prose and fonts outweigh every line of code), and who occupies the bytes after tree-shaking (the machine the router wraps is 22.5% of the bundle; the router itself, 3.9%). Sheet 11 cuts the same wire the other way, pricing five package quarters and sixteen doors one at a time. Sheet 12 leaves the wire and draws the monorepo as its own CI reads it, the pull-request task graph punched onto a register plate. Sheet 13 ages the city by commit date, and sheet 14 turns the instrument on itself: the census pipeline behind almost every number here, drawn as archive → probe stations → filed plates → drawings and introspected from the generator at build time. Interactive lanes (1i, 2B, 12i, 14i and the three.js city) walk the plates they sit beside; the appendix files plates whose subject is the atlas rather than the codebase.

FILES — diagrams/ holds each sheet standalone, megacanvas.html, and this gallery. DRAWN BY FABLE (CLAUDE, AI) FOR SHANE DANIEL.
cover.thesis: Riffs on an isometric codebase-visualization form seen in the wild; the notes on each sheet argue where that form fits and where it lies.
cover.notes: Static HTML pages, written by node generator/build.mjs . from this directory. The SVG sheets need nothing; the interactive plates (1i, 2B, 12i, 14i, 7·3D) load cytoscape 3.31.0 and three.js 0.169.0 from cdnjs, which generator/stage-site.mjs vendors for hosting. app/ is the same set as a prerendered lit-ui-router app; build.mjs emits its fragments and manifest. On the published site the app owns the root (/, /sheet/7, /city) and this flat set is staged beside it under /set/ as the version to compare against; the two link to each other (the app's rail and crumbs, the gallery's cover). Light theme is graphite-on-vellum; dark is cyanotype. Since 2026-09-06 every label on the plates draws in the data face (DIN 2014, Barlow Semi Condensed off the kit) rather than the system monospace; mono is reserved for code. Generated 2026-08-16 by Fable (Claude, AI). Every plate in data/ — versions, dates and all — was re-counted at origin/main @ 185d414 in one pass, plate 7A's test light included: generator/census-shadow.mjs re-meters it at the same ref. The cover's general survey — every tracked file on the scc 4.0.0 Code basis, origin/main @ 185d414 — is imported from data/census-files.json, the master snapshot generator/census-scc.mjs writes; generator/census-overview.mjs prints the same rollup on the terminal.

sheets.title: THE RENDER LOOP
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 1 — lit-ui-router 1.11.2 · the client circuit drawn as one isometric scene: every leg of the loop is a road on the grid, the document a browser window whose DOM rises in plates, and the five package entries a door strip along the footer · version read from census-files.json
sheets.caption: The loop sits on the ground: every leg is a road that turns along the iso axes and stops short of the wall it points at. The city breaks its metaphor once, on purpose — the document is not a building but a browser window whose DOM rises in plates. The core matches, the hall runs its hook bays, Lit commits onto a layer, and a click on the topmost plate flies back to location.
sheets.verdict: strong fit — the render cycle is a genuine circuit

sheets.title: THE RENDER LOOP, WALKED
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 1 — sheet 1's circuit, stepped · one navigation walked leg by leg · 10 STATIONS · 12 LEGS · 12 STEPS · surveyed at origin/main @ 185d414 (commit 2026-09-06)
sheets.caption: The circuit, stood up and stepped. 10 stations and 12 legs, then one click — a click on <a uiSref> from /people to /people/32 — walked in 12 steps under the pointer, every step standing on the 30 source lines the plate cites verbatim.
sheets.verdict: sheet 1's circuit with a pointer in it — 10 stations, 12 legs, and one click walked in 12 steps, every step standing on the source lines the plate cites verbatim

sheets.title: THE BRICK ASSEMBLY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 2 — one baseplate, four bricks, 27 authored files · an exploded LEGO assembly with every coupling named to the API call that makes it, brick and stud faces drawn opaque so nothing reads through a mass in front of it · source counted at origin/main @ 185d414 (2026-09-07)
sheets.caption: Every companion enters through a published stud on @uirouter/core, and no two of them touch. Drawn exploded, the sheet answers the only question that matters about a plugin architecture: pull any brick off and what breaks? Nothing — the studs stay where they are.
sheets.verdict: exploded: every coupling is a published stud on core — and the server takes none

sheets.caption: The monorepo drawn as what it functionally is: a short conveyor that turns source into one tarball, inside a yard of instruments built to measure that tarball. Every structure carries its measured mass — footprint ∝ √sloc, height ∝ authored files — and gate severity is colour rather than height, because the two do not correlate: the blocks that stop the line are among the smallest on the sheet.

sheets.title: THE HANDOFF WORKS
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3 · ALTERNATE PLATE — the sheet-3 task-manager inset at full size: 8 of 11 workflows · 49 mise tasks in 4 homes · turbo ci 605 nodes, 183 real · 4 seam types · 3 service doors · every frame sized to the widest DIN line it holds, so the spine is computed rather than hand-set · every count imported from diagrams/data/census-handoff.json + census-plate.json · counted at origin/main @ 185d414 (2026-09-07)
sheets.caption: The two task managers drawn as the two machines they are — mise the node-free umbrella, turbo the cached fan-out — with the seams as the featured parts: every crossing is a bolted gasket labeled with what crosses it and what the boundary buys. The star fitting is the cache gasket on the return duct: turbo caches mise, because the six re-entrant lint lanes hash the mise task files and mise.lock, so a tool-pin bump invalidates exactly its own lane.
sheets.verdict: turbo caches mise — and the loop is a DAG in a loop costume: the 7 tasks that shell turbo and the 8 turbo re-enters never touch; every count imported, turbo at 98 definitions in 17 files

sheets.title: THE WATCHED CITY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3 · ALTERNATE PLATE B — the PR ci graph as a city: 183 real tasks in 28 massed structures · footprint = watched files (46,781 task-file hashes) · height = command sloc (2,118) · 422 phantom plots · every number imported from diagrams/data/census-mass3b.json, surveyed at origin/main @ 185d414 (2026-09-07)
sheets.caption: The pull-request graph that plate 3A traced as plumbing, surveyed here as ground: every real task massed by what it watches (footprint) and what it actually executes (height). The survey’s verdict is flatness — 143 of 183 blocks are a single script line riding an external binary — which makes the exceptions legible at a glance: a 291-line test tower on a 32-file lot, a 70-line patch check on a 646-file lot, a 31,866-file plain patrolled by 25 lines of command, and a 401-sloc spire over the root lint lane that runs this repo's own bin instead of an external one.

sheets.title: THE FAMILY SPINE

sheets.caption: Not a loop and not a city: a spine. Every limb shares @uirouter/core and no limb talks to another, so the honest drawing is radial. Each block is massed from its own authored source and each stem crosses a gate naming the core range that limb admits — and the gates do not agree.
sheets.verdict: every limb re-massed from sloc × files — one red gate: @uirouter/react pins core as a dependency

sheets.caption: No mechanism connects these projects, so any drawn edge would be fiction. What is real is position: where matching happens, who owns navigation, and — the one square — whether the URL or a state tree is the source of truth.

sheets.title: THE MEASURED CITY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3½ — the same city as sheet 3, surveyed by mass · 32 members in 4 districts, footprint ∝ √sloc, height ∝ authored files, spec mass drawn as an annex, gate severity in colour · counted at origin/main @ 185d414 (2026-09-07)
sheets.caption: Sheet 3 drew the monorepo as a process; this sheet counts who lives in it. Footprint ∝ √sloc, height ∝ authored files, tests drawn as annexes rather than deleted — and over that census the two things a census alone cannot say: which district each member belongs to, and which roads run between them. Every road is a workspace dependency or a turbo task edge, never an impression.
sheets.verdict: the census with districts and roads — tests as annexes, every edge cited: the 8-line harness stops every PR, and all 32 members are measured on the scc ruler

sheets.title: THE SHADOW SURVEY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3½ — ALTERNATE PLATE TO SHEET 7: the measured city under its own test light · same city as sheet 7, 32 members · reach = the source each suite loads, brightness = line coverage of what it loads · metered at origin/main @ 185d414 (2026-09-07)
sheets.caption: Sheet 7 counted who lives in the city; this plate asks which of them ever stand in test light. Every member’s own suite is run under a coverage meter, and its light drawn to two rules: reach is how much of the member’s source the suite actually loads, brightness is the line coverage of what it loads. What the suite never imports stays in shadow — and the finding is a repo-wide habit visible from the air: the light is bright far more often than it is wide. Where a suite reaches, it burns near-full; what it never touches is simply dark.
sheets.verdict: the shadow survey — the tests are the light: where a suite reaches it burns near-full — 17 members read under their own suites' meters at 185d414, so the light and the census are one measurement

sheets.title: THE WORKING CITY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3½ — SYNTHESIS PLATE TO SHEET 7: the census city as a working plant · weathering (13) × test light (7A) × gates (7) × live build, one sprite per member · steam window 2026-06-09..2026-09-06 · counted at origin/main @ 185d414 (2026-09-07)
sheets.caption: Sheet 7 counted the city, sheet 13 dated its stone, plate 7A metered its test light. This plate turns the same city on: every member becomes a Working Plant sprite in the Factorio sense — a machine whose state is broadcast, not implied. Rust speckle for idleness, steam for the last ninety days of commits, module lamps for test light, pipes for the build. The channels are independent on purpose, and the city proves they must be: the flagship runs at full steam under every lamp while wearing rust, and the most-rusted machine in the yard is still quietly steaming. The alert channel is drawn and empty: no gate in the city is red at HEAD.
sheets.verdict: the synthesis plate — rust, steam, lamps and pipes on one city: 31 plants run and every pipe connects on 24 green build tasks, 16 carry metered lamps, and the alert register stands drawn and empty — no gate is red at HEAD

sheets.title: THE WEATHERING MAP
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE t — the same city as sheet 7, surveyed in time · 319 files dated from the whole history · three construction seasons, 10 silent months · counted at origin/main @ 185d414
sheets.caption: Every sheet so far has drawn the city as it stands; this one dates the stone. Same districts, same footprints as sheet 7 — but the fills now say when each file was first committed and the edges say how often it is touched. The history turns out to be three construction campaigns separated by silent months, and the two encodings disagree on purpose: 86% of the city is summer-built and barely weathered, while the port’s original masonry — 26 files from July 2025 — carries the hottest edges on the map.
sheets.verdict: 86% of the city is summer stone — and the port’s original masonry, 26 files from 2025-07-21, carries the hottest edges

appendix.title: THE SPRITE STUDY
appendix.sub: APPENDIX · META — the research behind the building sprites, drawn in the set it argues about · three concepts on one demo member, five states each · the reference strip of game screenshots is cited in the notes rather than drawn, because the atlas draws no images
appendix.caption: Every other plate in this set measures the codebase. This one measures a decision: how a workspace member should look when a sheet draws it as a building. One demo member — 16 files, 1,900 sloc, massed under the same rules sheet 7 uses — is drawn fifteen times, five states along a wreck-to-splendor gauge under three competing treatments, and each treatment is priced. The verdict stands in the set: sheet 7B is the working plant, and sheet 13 is the weathering gauge those studies were commissioned for.
appendix.verdict: meta — the research behind the building sprites, argued on one demo member in fifteen blocks: the working plant wins on cost and independence and shipped as sheet 7B, the vines are its second layer, and the ledger roof stays parked until a sheet wants per-file stories
